title: code-review-pr-notes-kv-cache-batching-refactor
content:
PR: #2345 — KV cache + batching refactor (WIP)
Author: @ameliar
Goal: Reduce tail latency for short-chat workloads by improving KV cache hit stability and making batching less sensitive to request size variance.

Quick summary:
- Introduces new KVCacheLayer that centralizes prefix caching and eviction policy.
- Changes batching heuristics: now uses dynamic batch window based on percentiles of recent seq lengths instead of fixed time buckets.
- Adds a batching estimator to predict token generation length (basic heuristic) to reduce padding.
- Removes per-request fallback path that forced sync flush on miss (this was a big perf hit).

High-level concerns / things to check:
- Correctness: ensure we never serve stale KV cache entries across model versions (pinning/version tags missing?).
- Thread-safety: shared cache access needs locks or sharded atomics — current impl uses a single mutex around reads (scales poorly).
- Memory: eviction policy currently LRU with global size cap. For long seq workloads this can OOM — consider size-aware eviction (bytes not entries).
- Metrics: a bunch of new counters added but no dashboards. Need latency-by-route and hit-rate histograms.
- Tests: unit tests for eviction, race tests for concurrent access, integration perf test for batching heuristics.

Review checklist (what I'm using when scanning):
- [ ] API surface unchanged (no breaking changes for callers)
- [ ] Model version pinning present in cache keys (model_name:version:prefix_hash)
- [ ] Eviction respects max_bytes not just max_entries
- [ ] No blocking sync I/O on hot path
- [ ] Proper metrics emitted (kv_cache.hit, kv_cache.miss, batch.size, batch.wait_time)
- [ ] Benchmarks added (ci/bench/kvcache) and PR includes sample numbers
- [ ] Adequate comments on heuristics + link to design doc

Notes on specific files:
- kvcache/kv_cache.py: new LRUMap wrapper — missing size accounting. TODO: add byte_size bookkeeping on set().
- serving/batcher.py: dynamic window logic OK but uses global recent_lengths list. For high QPS this will be a contention hotspot — suggest ring buffer per-shard.
- serving/fallbacks.py: removed sync flush but left the old code commented — remove before merge (clean).
- tests/test_kvcache_eviction.py: good start, but add scenario with mixed small/huge entries to validate size-based eviction.

Performance notes from local runs (macbook M1 -> approx numbers, need CI GPU runs):
- baseline (main): p95 latency for short-chat (<=128 tokens) = 42ms
- PR branch (local): p95 = 28ms (improvement) but p99 sometimes spikes to 600ms when eviction GC runs
- memory: heap growth observed in long seq test (2000 tokens) — suspect leak in ring-buffer copy on resizing

Suggested refactors / action items:
- Replace single global mutex with sharded locks (consistent hashing on prefix) — low risk, big win for throughput.
- Switch eviction policy to size-aware LRU and run through stress tests.
- Move dynamic batching state to per-worker shard (avoid global recent_lengths).
- Add a background compaction/GC that runs incrementally, not full stop-the-world.

Tests to add before merging:
- race_kvcache_concurrent_reads_writes (1000 threads simulated)
- eviction_size_mixed_entries (verify bytes freed, not just entries)
- batching_variance_stability (simulate mixed seq length stream and assert p99 < threshold)
- integration_perf_ci (small nightly job that runs on dedicated infra with a sample workload)

Questions for author / follow-ups:
- Did you consider using jemalloc statistics for more accurate memory accounting?
- Are model version tags populated for all entry writes? If not, adding this is critical to avoid cross-version contamination.
- Can we get some CI runs on dedicated infra with GPUs for realistic p99 numbers?

Notes to self:
- Follow up with @ravi about making a mini-dashboard for kv_cache metrics (low effort, high visibility).
- Open JIRA for size-aware eviction: INF-4620 (todo)
- If we can't get stable p99, fallback strategy: auto-disable caching for routes with high seq variance via route policy.

WIP markings in code: search for "// WIP-PERF" and "// TODO-REFACTOR" — leave comments inline.

Final thought: overall design is promising, measurable improvements in p95 seen locally. Main blockers are memory accounting and GC spikes at p99. If author addresses sharding + size-eviction + CI perf runs, I think this can land.

-- end --
